newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian Ramadan leaves trail of dead and maimed.
newsitem.headline: Algerian Ramadan leaves trail of dead and maimed.

text.p: Algeria on Saturday concluded the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan marked by the bloodiest sustained guerrilla violence in five years of conflict.
The deadly campaign combined night massacres of civilians in hamlets around Algiers with car bomb attacks in the Algerian capital and surrounding cities.

It reached its political climax 18 days after the start of Ramadan on January 10 when gunmen, said by the authorities to be Moslem fundamentalists, shot dead Algeria's top union leader Abdelhak Benhamouda in central Algiers.
The Algerian Jihad Islamic Front (FIDA), a little known small faction based in Algiers, claimed responsibility in killing Benhamouda, who was a staunch political backer of President Liamine Zeroual.

Between 250 and 300 people, and maybe more, died in the violence in Ramadan, according to Algerian official and newspaper reports. They included a 13-month-old baby, a strangled boy, 12, and five girls who had their throats cut.
The fundamentalist Armed Islamic Group had promised to step up attacks during Ramadan, seeing the period as most fitted for their struggle to try to topple Zeroual's government.
Following is a list of the main violence in that period:
Jan 12
- Moslem guerrillas kill 14 villagers in Tabainat hamlet, in Blida province, 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers.
- The same day they kidnap five girls and cut their throats in the neighbouring village of Haouch Englise.
Jan 14
- Nine bodies are found in Djebel Koukou in Algiers and Bab Ali village, near Algiers, according to Algerian newspapers.
Jan 16
- At least four guerrillas killed in a seven-hour gunbattle with security forces on the heights of Algiers's ancient Casbah. Residents say more than 10 died. Authorities say nothing.
- Bomb explodes in a car market in Boufarik, 30 km (20 miles) south of Algiers killing 12 people and wounding scores, according to the authorities. Newspapers put the dead at 14.
Jan 19
- Car bomb explodes on Algiers's Belouizdad Street, Belcourt, killing 21 people and wounding 60, according to the authorities. Newspapers say 42 people were killed.
- Moslem guerrillas kill 36 people in Sidi Abdelaziz village, in Medea province, 70 km (40 miles) south of Algiers, according to the authorities. Newspapers put the toll at 48.
Jan 20
- Bomb explodes by girls school in Algiers. No casualties.
Jan 21
- Car bomb explodes in Boulevard des Martyrs, killing six people and wounding 44. Five hours later another blast kills one near children's merry-go-round in another part of Algiers.
Jan 22
- Bomb explodes in a market in central Blida killing eight and wounding 10, government-run El Moudajhid newspaper said.
- Car bomb kills seven and wounds scores in Quatre Chemins hamlet, near Boufarik, according to Liberte newspaper.
Jan 26
- Gunmen kill Said Rabhi, grassroots activist from hawkish anti-Islamist Rally for Democracy and Culture in Kouba, Algiers.
Jan 28
- Moslem guerrillas shoot dead top union leader Abdelhak Benhamouda by his Union Generale des Travailleurs Algeriens (UGTA) headquarters in central Algiers, interior ministry says.
Jan 30
- Former army general Habib Khelil killed in Oran, security forces says. El Watan newspaper says a gunman shot him in head.
- Eight people killed on Wednesday-Thursday night in Sidi Moussa area in Blida.
Feb 2
- El Watan newspaper said Moslem guerrillas slaughtered 31 people on Friday-Saturday night in Medea, south of Algiers.
Feb 3
- Seven people killed on Saturday-Sunday night in Benoir Louz hamlet near Larba, some 25 km (15 miles) south of Algiers. Security officials blame guerrillas.
Feb 4
- Suspected Moslem guerrillas massacre whole family by hacking off the heads of its nine members on Monday-Tuesday night, Al Khabar and El Watan newspapers said.
- Liberte newspaper says security forces killed 28 guerrillas in the past week.
